+## Spec conflicts / spec gaps
+
+1. BillFn is intent, not a production specification. It lacks requirement IDs, acceptance tests, tenant keys, provider webhook protocols, idempotency boundaries, data retention, migration/rollback, error taxonomy, caps, SLOs, and release gates.
+2. BillFn package naming conflicts with current root rules: intent uses @billfn/* and @uifn/billing while the repository guide reserves unscoped names for single-function packages and @superfunctions/* for shared packages. Resolve ownership before implementation.
+3. ExtFn formal requirements name @superfunctions/extfn-* while implementation publishes @extfn/*. This is a direct consumption/release contract conflict.
+4. ExtFn calls outputPath a manifest path while Vite preserves HTML input directories. The spec needs one canonical rule for input identity, emitted file location, hashed assets, and manifest reference validation.
+5. ExtFn describes persistent ports across MV3 suspension without specifying lease/reconnect/replay/subscription ownership or delivery guarantees. In-memory reconnection cannot satisfy it.
+6. LangFn formal caps in SPEC conflict with implementation defaults: ToolAgent 8 versus 5, ReAct 12 versus 10, plan 24 versus 10, graph 256 versus 100, DB scan 100 versus 512, and trace max 500 versus HTTP 100. One generated constants source should govern both languages.
+7. LangFn says HTTP supports tenant headers but does not clearly state that authenticated identity must dominate them. Treat headers as trusted only after an explicit gateway attestation; otherwise reject mismatch.
+8. LangFn promises safe outbound policy but does not define DNS resolution, redirect revalidation, IPv4-mapped IPv6, alternate loopback names, proxy behavior, or allowlist-mandatory production mode.
+9. LogFn declares secure-by-default redaction while separately describing default pipeline as empty. Security intent must win: safe presets should be the default, with explicit opt-out.
+10. LogFn WatchFn handler accepts optional auth even though transport-auth and server-ingest validation are acceptance/security criteria. Production and development modes need explicit separate constructors.
+11. MemoryFn container tag semantics are ambiguous between any-overlap and scope identity; using overlap for authorization is unsafe. Tenant and immutable container identity must be separate mandatory predicates.
+12. MemoryFn spec lists four backends and broad APIs but gives no capability matrix, transaction semantics, migration ownership, consistency model, or degraded-mode policy.
+13. UserFn is explicitly a draft/not-started spec while a published-looking SDK exists. Release metadata must label the SDK experimental until the service and security architecture exist.
+14. UserFn rich-text/Markdown content lacks a sanitizer and allowed CTA protocol/origin contract; arbitrary admin-authored HTML/URLs are unsafe by default.
+15. Several functions are omitted from root workspaces/release gates, so local package-level success and repository release success are different claims. Formal specs must name their canonical root commands.

+## Cross-cutting audits
+
+### Security and trust boundaries
+
+- Critical tenant breach: MemoryFn search has no tenant predicate and MCP searches with an empty scope. Any exposed MCP or HTTP composition can cross tenants. This is an architectural release stop, not a missing test.
+- Critical stored XSS: UserFn toast interpolates persisted campaign title/body into innerHTML. Admin-supplied content must be treated as untrusted, sanitized or rendered through text/approved Markdown nodes, with CSP-compatible behavior.
+- LangFn identity spoof: request tenant/user headers precede authenticated session claims. All authorization, budgets, rate keys, trace metadata, and storage scopes can be charged to or read under another identity if downstream trusts this context.
+- SSRF: LangFn blocks only selected literal IPv4 hosts. Production tools need explicit host allowlists, DNS resolution and post-connect verification, redirect rechecks, IPv6/IPv4-mapped handling, proxy policy, byte/time caps, and response sanitization.
+- LogFn leaks by default: adapters pass an empty redaction list, while the safer middleware helper list is bypassed. Default log presets must remove Authorization, Cookie, API-key, token, and configurable PII fields before any sink.
+- BillFn has no trust model at all. Payment/provider implementation must not start until principal, tenant, secret, webhook, replay, and ledger invariants are normative.
+
+### Correctness, determinism, and concurrency
+
+- ExtFn deterministic output is still invalid output: generated manifests must be checked against emitted files as a release assertion for every target/example.
+- MemoryFn extraction returning an empty list is indistinguishable from successful extraction of no facts; add should preserve original content or fail explicitly. Multi-write memory/relationship/latest-state updates require one transaction and deterministic mapping.
+- LogFn HTTP retry must allocate an attempt-scoped AbortController/timer, stop on permanent 4xx, honor Retry-After, retain durable offline batches, and surface drop metrics. Current behavior can retry permanent errors, run later attempts without timeout, and lose unload data.
+- UserFn delivery counts are campaign-global process memory, not per user/session and not restart-safe. Frequency caps need atomic durable keys and reconciliation.
+- LangFn cancellation must propagate AbortSignal to provider transports; racing a promise changes the caller result but leaves cost-producing work running.
+
+### Limits and resource safety
+
+- LangFn omits most formal prompt/chat/tool/batch/template/tag/feedback/trace/body ceilings. Enforce shared constants before allocation and provider calls in both languages.
+- MemoryFn has no body/content/query/tag/limit/embedding-dimension caps. Empty/global vector search and arbitrary MCP limit can exhaust the database.
+- LogFn 64KiB uses UTF-16 string length and never verifies the final UTF-8 serialized bytes. Middleware body and WatchFn batch event-size caps also need enforcement.
+- UserFn lacks campaign/survey content limits, event queue limits, submission/rate caps, attachment limits, and public-board moderation budgets.
+- ExtFn needs payload byte/depth caps at the real browser transport plus content anchor/mutation bounds to avoid host-page CPU/DOM amplification.
+
+### Errors and observability
+
+- Returning success after dropping data appears in MemoryFn extraction, UserFn feedback/track, and LogFn WatchFn ingest. Acknowledgement must mean durable acceptance, with operation/event IDs and queryable outcomes.
+- Health/readiness is missing or dependency-incomplete across the cohort. Readiness must await schema/migrations, storage, providers, browser build validation, and background worker recovery.
+- Console logging of feedback, memory content, or provider errors is not structured/redacted observability. Use LogFn/WatchFn only after fixing their secure defaults and durable ingest.
+- Interfaces and hooks do not prove operational readiness. None of these functions supplies alert rules, recovery runbooks, queue-age/error-budget metrics, or a live SLO report.
+
+### Packaging, compatibility, and release
+
+- ExtFn local package suites/builds/examples are meaningful but package identities contradict the spec and real-browser/store proof is absent.
+- LangFn has the strongest release gate in this cohort; 71 Python tests and TypeScript checks passed. Its security and contract failures remain blockers despite the green gate.
+- LogFn TypeScript is green locally; Python default pytest depends on an undeclared local tool installation at runtime and parity is unsafe/lossy.
+- MemoryFn and UserFn are omitted from root workspaces, so root Turbo cannot protect them. Their package manifests also advertise surfaces or readiness beyond implementation.
+- No cohort demonstrated npm pack/wheel installation from an empty consumer, registry contents, supported-version matrices, database upgrade/rollback, signed provenance, or release artifact SBOM/advisory disposition.
+
+## Recommendations
+
+### P0 — release stop
+
+1. Keep all six functions unreleased for production use. Label BillFn absent, MemoryFn/UserFn prototype, and the other four pre-release until blockers close.
+2. MemoryFn: require authenticated server-derived tenant/container scope on every API/MCP/storage operation; add tenant equality to all queries and uniqueness keys; reject empty scope; write cross-tenant negative tests for TS/Python.
+3. UserFn: remove innerHTML interpolation, sanitize the approved rich-text subset, allow only explicit CTA schemes/origins, and add CSP/DOM XSS regression tests.
+4. LangFn: make authenticated subject authoritative, reject header mismatch, require fail-closed auth in production composition, and harden outbound requests across DNS/IPv6/redirect/proxy boundaries.
+5. LogFn: enable redaction/masking by default, make production WatchFn ingest authenticated and durable, repair HTTP retry/timeout/offline semantics, and never acknowledge discarded data.
+6. ExtFn: validate every manifest path against emitted artifacts, implement real browser runtime messaging/events/ports, and add MV3 suspension/restart recovery tests in Chromium and Firefox.
+
+### P1 — release candidate
